# Theme-guide lifecycle instrument: bounded preparation

## Resume contract

- Packet: R3, owner-funded theme-guide maintenance; actual Gallery Synthwave is the
  named workload. Existing memory-v2 metrics cannot establish frame/isolate ownership.
- Smallest deliverable: opt-in guarded lifecycle tracing and a bounded, raw-evidence
  checkpoint collector, with synthetic failure controls. No runtime optimization,
  new framework, consumer change or retrospective v1 pass.
- Inputs: clean app-kit main `45bae1e6534c9fc91cc7f6e5db749d525bfac2e4`; preserve its
  stash and earlier receipts. Local protocol definitions are the same selected file
  documented in the [v2 contract](fixtures/styleguide-performance/memory-v2-contract.md).
- Authority: kit code/docs, synthetic tests, reviewed kit commit/push. No consumer,
  dependency, installed tool, global config, daemon restart, real data or deployment.
- Acceptance: preserve valid default command setup; unknown targets and failed
  instrumentation commands prevent resume; capture raw target/frame/context/loader/isolate data
  before release; checkpoint refuses context/target/session drift and retains partial
  failures. Recorded observations are not independent attribution or retention proof.
- Cost cap: two economical agents (bounded implementation and independent review),
  one initial synthetic round plus two repair rounds per module, roughly45minutes.
  Zero browser runs in this preparatory increment. The subsequent qualified method
  retains v2's one-positive/one-retention-control cap; no full matrix is authorized
  by unit success. Preserve executed source before any repair.
- Return: instrumentation in app-kit, fixed v2 follow-up and evidence here. No CUE
  readiness promotion. Human A/B, cancellation/cache and whole-app memory stay open.

Review also exposed malformed/duplicate attachment handling in the existing guard.
All modes now reject those identities before session commands/map replacement, retain
their raw metadata and refuse voluntary detach when attachment liveness is unknown.
The external owner must terminate its browser in that case. Pending setup cannot
resume a target after the guard has failed. This hardening changes invalid-input
handling, not the valid default command sequence or application permissions.

## Claims boundary

The collector records browser observations, not a proof that all allocations belong
to the guide. Session detachment is not target destruction. A context-destroyed event
is not evidence that its memory was reclaimed. Endpoint frame trees and isolate IDs
cannot exclude retained detached isolates or native/image/GPU allocations.

Independent lifecycle joining and a real, deliberately retained allocation control
are still required before accepting attribution. The actual native task, twenty
cycles, five-second idle endpoints, process sampling, body/ZIP verification and owner
cleanup remain separate, unchanged requirements of the v2 contract.

Checkpoint success means recorded observations with matching command/response IDs,
methods, sessions and raw results. It is not independent qualification. Its five-second
acceptance deadline begins at entry and is rechecked around synchronous work as well
as awaited reads; synchronous Node work is not preempted. The process owner must still
apply its watchdog. The two inventories and repeated reads are not an atomic snapshot.

## Next bounded action

Build the independent lifecycle join over these raw events, explicitly exposing
shared/unobserved/retired ownership. Freeze it with the exact guide/control acquisition,
then qualify the separate native-navigation and deliberately retained >4MiB controls
before interpreting one guide cell. Preserve v2's acquisition cap and stop at the
first unknown-target, identity or containment failure. Retention/lifetime coverage,
twenty-cycle native tasks, process accounting and owner cleanup cannot be replaced
by this instrument's successful unit tests. No automatic full matrix or consumer rollout.

Records consulted: root intent/invariants/autonomy, R3 and ADR-0073. No attribution
revisit trigger has fired, no ADR was superseded and no runtime API is changed.
